member.name: T:Filee.Core.Conversion.ConversionEdge
member.summary: One direct conversion a converter can perform, e.g. docx → pdf.
member.param: Source format id.
Target format id. May equal (e.g. re-encode a JPG at lower quality).
Relative cost used by . Use 10 for a normal direct conversion, higher for lossy or slow paths. Multi-step routes add up their costs.
The edge is used only in routes that start from a raster image (): image tracing may follow ICNS → PNG, but must never redraw a PDF, a vector drawing or a video frame that became a PNG.

The opposite: never used in routes that start from a raster image. PDF → SVG through LibreOffice keeps a PDF's vectors, but a photo that became a PDF would only come back as a picture inside an SVG, so images are traced.

The edge is a route of its own only: the file being converted is a file and is what the user asked for. PDF → PPTX puts pictures of the pages on slides; a Word document rendered to PDF must not become pictures on slides, and a picture deck must not be a step towards ODP or PPSX.

The edge writes every frame of a video as numbered pictures into a folder (). It is never part of an ordinary route (a video → JPG stays one still frame), and with asking for frames it is the whole route.

The engine draws text one character after the other, left to right, without complex-script shaping (no joined Arabic letters, no right-to-left order, no reordered vowel signs, conjuncts or placed marks). A source whose text needs shaping is never routed through the edge: asks the engine () and plans again without it. Text the engine draws but has no widths for (letters outside ASCII and Latin-1 other than full-width CJK — Polish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Greek, Cyrillic — rhwp#8143) takes a route without the edge only when one exists.

The edge takes the video out of a Live / Motion Photo (). It is never part of an ordinary route (a photo → MP4 is otherwise a video of the still picture), and with asking for it it is the whole route.
The edge makes a Live / Motion Photo of a short clip of a video (). It is never part of an ordinary route (a video → JPG is otherwise one still frame), and with asking for it it is the whole route.
The edge recognizes the text of a scan or a picture and writes a searchable PDF (). It is never part of an ordinary route, and with asking for it the route starts with it.
The edge transcribes speech to SRT subtitles or plain text using Whisper ().

The edge writes a file's metadata changes into a copy of it in its own format, the picture, sound or document itself left as it is (, ExifTool). It is never part of an ordinary route, and with asking for it it is the whole route.

The edge is used only in routes that start from one of these formats (ids, lower case); null for every source. WeasyPrint's HTML → PDF serves pages, Markdown and e-mails, which become HTML first, but must not become a hop for a Word document or an e-book that the HTML writers could also turn into a page.

member.summary: "Move the original to the Recycle Bin / Trash" (, #1387): once every result of is complete and none has the source's format, the source goes to the Trash. A result of the source's own format is "Replace the original"'s, and a result at the source's own path would be moved with it, so either leaves the source alone. When the Trash refuses, the source stays and the file gets a note saying why; nothing is ever deleted for good.

member.name: M:Filee.Core.Gallery.GalleryIndex.RelativePath
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(?:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_\\-]*/){0,3}presets/(?<id>[a-z0-9\\-]{3,48})/(?<file>preset\\.json|images/(?:[A-Za-z]{2,3}(?:-[A-Za-z]{2,4})?/)?[1-4](?:-thumb)?\\.[a-z]{3,4})$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Loop greedily at most 3 times.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [-0-9_a-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match the string "presets/".
○ "id" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [-0-9a-z] atomically at least 3 and at most 48 times.
○ Match '/'.
○ "file" capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "preset.json".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "images/".
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match a character in the set [A-Za-z] greedily at least 2 and at most 3 times.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a character in the set [A-Za-z] atomically at least 2 and at most 4 times.
○ Match '/'.
○ Match a character in the set [1-4].
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match the string "-thumb".
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a character in the set [a-z] atomically at least 3 and at most 4 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

Pattern:
^([1-4])(?:(-thumb)\\.webp|\\.(png|jpg|jpeg|webp))$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [1-4].
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match the string "-thumb".
○ Match the string ".webp".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match '.'.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "png".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "jp".
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match 'g'.
○ Match the string "eg".
○ Match the string "webp".
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.summary: Sorts . Names sort the way people count ("page 2" before "page 10", see ), with the full path deciding between equal names. Files with equal dates sort by name, and files without a date come last in both directions: they have no place on the timeline. With the name is the whole path, in Explorer's order: each folder's files stay together, sub folders before files. For files from one folder tree, that is the order of their relative paths.

member.summary: "Ask every time" (#521): the donut asks where to save first, once per batch, in the source's folder (). Where nothing can ask (the command line, files from a browser, other tools), applies. A bool of its own, so a Filee from before it keeps the preset and uses Location.

member.summary: With : a source inside this folder keeps its subfolder below (Inbox\2025\a.jpg → converted\2025\a.pdf), so files of the same name in different subfolders don't end up side by side as a.pdf and a (2).pdf. Empty: everything goes straight into . Watch folders set it to the watched folder.

member.summary: Give converted files the creation and modification dates of their source, e.g. so converted photos still sort by when they were taken. Not for merged PDFs or combined archives, which come from many files.

member.summary: The folder "next to the source" means for this job, instead of the source's own: files dragged from a browser are saved there (or, when only the converted file is kept, into a work folder that is deleted afterwards). Set per job, never saved with a preset.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Presets.OutputRule.ZipResult
member.summary: Pack what a conversion writes for one file (a Shapefile's .shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj and .cpg, or a single file) into one ZIP named by the rule, instead of leaving the files themselves. The ZIP is the only output.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Presets.OutputRule.OnlyIfSmaller
member.summary: "Compress" presets: when a file that keeps its format doesn't get smaller, the output is a copy of the source instead, with a notice. A result in another format is always kept.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Presets.OutputRule.ReplaceOriginal
member.summary: The result takes the original's place and the original goes to the Recycle Bin / Trash (#332): only when the result has the source's format, only after it is complete, never for watch folders or files from a browser. When the original can't be moved there (a network drive, a file still open elsewhere, no Trash), it stays and the result is saved as usual, with a note saying why.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Presets.OutputRule.TrashOriginalAfterConvert
member.summary: The original goes to the Recycle Bin / Trash once its result is complete (#1387). Off by default. Where covers a result of the source's own format, this covers one in another format (DOCX → PDF). Never for watch folders, "Ask every time", files from a browser, the command line, merges and packing (a ZIP result, a combined archive), or an "Only if smaller" copy of the source. Only ever moved to the Recycle Bin / Trash, never deleted: when that isn't possible the original stays, with a note saying why.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Presets.OutputRule.MoveInsteadOfCopy
member.summary: Copy to folder only (#856): the files are moved into instead of copied, so they are gone from where they were. Off by default. An original is removed only once its copy is complete; files from a browser have no original and are saved as when copying. A Filee from before it ignores it and copies.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.ZipGeoResults

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.UiScale

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.NavCollapsed

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.MainWindow
member.summary: Where the main window was when it last closed, so the next start opens it there (#586). Null until it has closed once. A Filee from before it skips the property, so it needs no schema step.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.DonutPreviewPlace
member.summary: Where the Donut toolbar page's donut on screen was dragged to: its centre against the main window's top-left corner, in screen pixels (points on macOS) (, ), so it opens there beside the window again. Null until it has been dragged, and again once it is dropped onto the window. A Filee from before it skips the property, so it needs no schema step.

member.name: P:Filee.Core.Settings.AppSettings.TurnedOffFields
member.summary: The fields turned off on the Fields page (ids of ): a format that belongs only to them is left out of the donut and the preset lists. An empty list and a missing value both mean every field is on, so settings from before it read as every field on and need no schema step. A new install gets its defaults from .

member.name: M:Filee.Core.Settings.CustomTheme.Load(System.String,Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger)
member.summary: Reads theme.json from . Unknown names and values that are not hex colours are dropped (and logged); a missing, empty or unreadable file gives null, so Filee's own colours apply. The file is the user's: unlike settings.json it is never renamed or rewritten.

member.name: M:Filee.Core.Settings.CustomTheme.HexColor
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^#([0-9A-Fa-f]{6}|[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match '#'.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Fa-f] exactly 6 times.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Fa-f] exactly 8 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Filee.Core.Settings.UserDataStore.ResetProfile(Filee.Core.Profiles.ToolbarProfile)
member.summary: Puts one built-in donut back as a new library has it (name, slices of both faces and their order, extensions, normal or mixed) and leaves the other donuts alone. So no file type opens two donuts, an extension another normal donut takes now stays there. Presets are shared by every donut: the ones this donut drops stay in the library, edited ones keep their settings, and a built-in preset of its default slices that the user deleted comes back. A donut that changes kind moves to the border between the normal profiles and the mixed ones, the built-in mixed donut back to the head of the mixed ones (the catch-all).

member.name: M:Filee.Core.Web.WebDownloader.ConnectAsync(System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpConnectionContext,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Opens the connection to an address the name resolved to that isn't local. The check is made on the very addresses connected to, so a name that resolves to a public address once and a local one the next time (DNS rebinding) gets nowhere. A connection to the user's proxy is left alone: the proxy is their own choice. That is one to another address than the link's, or the handler's own CONNECT, which opens a tunnel to an https site through an http proxy: it names the proxy as its address, and a proxy on this computer (127.0.0.1:7890) would otherwise be refused. Downloads only ever send GET, so a CONNECT can only come from the proxy settings.
